exposure: Cesarean delivery at full dilatation in the first birth
outcome: Spontaneous preterm birth in the second pregnancy
cohort: Women with a first and second pregnancy recorded within the Aberdeen Maternity and Neonatal Databank between 1976 and 2017 (n=30,253)
finding: Cesarean delivery at full dilatation in the first birth was associated with a 3-fold increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth in the second pregnancy, even after adjusting for potential confounding factors.
mod_finding: Women with a previous cesarean delivery at full dilatation had a higher rate of repeat cesarean delivery at full dilatation (3.7%) and planned cesarean delivery (48%) in the second birth.
